decision: The tracked directive lists the whole scope: nine in-flight lanes, the QA pose and anatomy set, parity, gates, docs, publication and hygiene, each tied to an issue
why: Owner asked that the directive reflect the full and true scope; the repo had no directive.md so the stop hook saw a drained queue while 50+ issues were open
resolves: #89 #90 #91 #92 filed for scope that had no issue

decision: Animation frames travel on a framework-free channel owned by each PresenceRegistry (registry.frames): producers bind a figure id, a new binding supersedes the old one and raises a monotonic generation, observers get released/superseded notices, and interaction.observeFrames scopes a subscription to one session and ends with it
why: Figure ids are already presence ids and the interaction runtime already holds the registry, so one identity namespace serves gameplay, interaction and headless consumers; a standalone hub would be a second source of figure identity, and a React-only prop fails the no-renderer acceptance of #32

decision: The three retained legacy adult ids (genitals/penis-length, penis-circ, penis-testicles) count as shipped modifiers: 12 adult modifiers, 9 with sliders, 287 modifiers with the body pack's 275. Counts in README, introduction, llms.txt and the architecture notes are asserted against the manifests by tests/docsCounts.test.ts
why: The ids still evaluate and tests and saved recipes name them, so dropping them from the count would misstate what a recipe accepts; the source of truth is the manifests, not prose

decision: E2e specs read rendered pixels from compositor screenshots (e2e/lib/framePixels.ts, decoded with sharp), never by drawImage or readPixels of a WebGL canvas from a test script; preserveDrawingBuffer stays off on the creator, QA shot and walk canvases
why: c57d29cb turned the retained buffer off deliberately and moved creator.spec to screenshots; the other specs kept reading the cleared buffer, which failed 9 tests and could pass others vacuously. The screenshot is what people see, and restoring the buffer would reverse a recorded renderer decision to satisfy stale tests

decision: Every BVH over a hair card or the shared body triangles is built indirect through src/surface/meshBvh.ts, so it never reorders the caller's index and every query names a triangle in the caller's order
why: three-mesh-bvh sorts the index in place by default: hairFields read card hits as quad order and sampled the wrong cards' cut-out (162 of 324 vertices wrong in the test field), and hairFields, bindToBody and BodySurface reordered the model's own bodyControlTriangles. A copy plus a mapping per call site would repeat the bug at each new one

decision: Limits on the figure's fidelity are only ever the GPU's or the platform's, never a cap below what MakeHuman's model carries; where a limit forces a trade, the trade becomes an exposed quality setting developers dial toward speed or quality, not a constant. The 16-attribute WebGL budget is met by packing (hkFoldSlots, one attribute a component a joint), lossless. SKIN_INFLUENCES stays the pack's 8 (MakeHuman uses up to 12; 51 vertices exceed 8), and a runtime quality setting (influences used: 4 to 8) is the dial
why: Owner ruling 2026-10-13: align to the parent model's boundaries, expose optimisation as API. The 17-attribute body shader failed to link and hid every body; cutting the skin back would have traded MakeHuman parity for a GPU detail

decision: Body fluids are exempt from ruling 8 assets-only: thin films are material skin layers (sweat sheen, VULVA_MOISTURE_LAYER); moving fluid (beads, runs, drips, pooling, coagulation) is a simulated system with a per-fluid catalogue of rheology, optics and time behaviour
why: Owner ruling 2026-10-13: fluids move and cannot be assets; humans have many fluids with different behaviour (blood, pus, vomit, tears, sweat, saliva, urine, milk, genital fluids)

decision: humanoid-kit-adult-animations lives in this repository, age-gated beside packs/adult-anatomy (option a); all-ages self-contact clips live in the core
why: Owner directed adult self-interaction work (#117), settling scope; one age policy and one #22 audit in one repo beats splitting it; core still names no adult definition
